# Instructions

Complete all parts of the Exercises section below to earn a High Pass for this challenge.

**Requirements for high passing:**

Use tidyverse functions to do the following:

- Ex. 1 Calculate departure hour based on `dep_time` and calculate the most common hour.
- Ex. 2 Calculate the largest delay and then make an appropriate plot to show distribution.
- Ex. 3 Calculate average delay and proportion of missing values for each origin using the correct delay variable. Then calculate and show which origin airport had longest delay and most missing values.
- Ex. 4 Ccalculate IQR and then calculate/show which desintation airport had largest variability.
- Ex. 5 Calculate average dep delay per hour and show plot of relationship with previous hour.
- Ex. 6 Ensure data quality by re-calculating departure delay and show which rows, if any, are not consistent.
- Ex. 7 Calculate the fraction of flights that have any delay by weekday and show which day has the fewest delayed flights, proportionally.
- Ex. 8 Make an appropriate, professional plot.
- Ex. 9 Make an appropriate, professional plot.

Push your changes to GitHub by midnight on the deadline. (GitHub classroom automatically creates a pull request for receiving feedback.) Note that your submission is incomplete without a **readable, rendered HTML** in addition to the qmd file.

## Flights

Install the `nycflights13` package for the data used in this exercise. You can look at the codebook for the `flights` dataset with `?flights`. Each case represents one flight from a NYC airport in 2013.

```{r load_flights_data}
library(tidyverse)
library(nycflights13)
data(flights)
```

Using the `flights` dataset, complete the following:

1. What is the most common departure hour? Use the `dep_time` variable.

```{r}
flights_dep_hour <- flights %>%
  na.omit(dep_time)%>%
  mutate(dep_hour = str_sub(as.character(dep_time), start = 1, end = pmax(0, nchar(as.character(dep_time)) - 2)))%>% 
  mutate(dep_hour = as.numeric(dep_hour))%>%
  mutate(dep_hour = replace_na(dep_hour,0))%>%
  group_by(dep_hour)%>%
  summarise(count = n())%>%
  arrange(desc(count))

head(flights_dep_hour,1)
```
The most common departure hour is 8am.

2. Make a plot of the distribution of the largest delay for each flight (the larger of `dep_delay` and `arr_delay`).

```{r}
flights_delay<- flights%>%
  mutate(largest_delay = pmax(dep_delay, arr_delay, na.rm = TRUE))

ggplot()+
  geom_density(data =  flights_delay, aes(x=largest_delay))
```


3. Which `origin` airport had the longest average delay? Should you use `dep_delay` or `arr_delay` here? Which had the largest proportion of missing values for this delay variable?

```{r}
average_delays <- flights %>%
  group_by(origin) %>%
  summarize(mean_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_delay))

missing_proportions <- flights %>%
  group_by(origin) %>%
  summarize(
    missing_count = sum(is.na(dep_delay)),
    total_count = n(),
    missing_proportion = missing_count / total_count
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(missing_proportion))

head(average_delays,1)
head(missing_proportions,1)
```

EWR has the longest average delay. I used dep_delay, because origin is where the flight depart, which means it directly affect dep_delay rather than arr_delay. LGA has largest missing proportion.

4. Which destination (`dest`) airport had the largest variability in delays in terms of the difference between the 25th and 75th percentiles? Should you use `dep_delay` or `arr_delay` here?

```{r}
delay_variability <- flights %>%
  group_by(dest) %>%
  summarize(
    q25 = quantile(arr_delay, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = quantile(arr_delay, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr = q75 - q25
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(iqr))
head(delay_variability,1)
```
I used `arr_delay`, because destination only affect the arrival time.

5. Delays are typically temporally correlated: even once the problem that caused the initial delay has been resolved, later flights are delayed to allow earlier flights to leave. Use `lag()` to explore how the average departure delay for an hour is related to the average departure delay for the previous hour.

```{r}
hourly_delays <- flights %>%
  group_by(departure_datetime = floor_date(time_hour, unit = "hour")) %>%
  summarize(
    mean_delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
    count = n()
  ) %>%
  arrange(departure_datetime)%>%
  mutate(previous_mean_delay = lag(mean_delay))
ggplot(data = hourly_delays, aes(x=previous_mean_delay, y=mean_delay))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
```

There is a obvious relation that the delay will be higher in an hour when its previous hour has a high delay.

6. Compare `dep_time`, `sched_dep_time`, and `dep_delay`. Check the data quality of these three variables. Are they internally consistent with each other? If not, how are they not consistent?

```{r}
# calculated_delay <- flights %>%
#   mutate(cal_delay = dep_time - sched_dep_time)%>%
#   filter(dep_delay != cal_delay)

flights_fixed_delay <- flights %>%
  mutate(
    dep_time_mins = (dep_time %/% 100) * 60 + (dep_time %% 100),
    sched_dep_time_mins = (sched_dep_time %/% 100) * 60 + (sched_dep_time %% 100),
    dep_time_mins = if_else(dep_time == 2400, 0, dep_time_mins), 
    sched_dep_time_mins = if_else(sched_dep_time == 2400, 0, sched_dep_time_mins)
  ) %>%
  mutate(calculated_delay = dep_time_mins - sched_dep_time_mins) %>%
  mutate(calculated_delay = ifelse(abs(calculated_delay - dep_delay) > 720,
                                      ifelse(calculated_delay > 0,
                                             calculated_delay - 1440,
                                             calculated_delay + 1440),
                                   calculated_delay)) %>%
  mutate(diff = dep_delay - calculated_delay) %>%
  filter(!is.na(diff), diff != 0) 

flights_fixed_delay
```


'dep_time' and 'sched_dep_time' have same quality with HHMM or HMM, but 'dep_delay' is in minutes. Minutes will became a new hour when it reach 60, but HHMM and HMM are viewed as integers. For example, 600-554 in HMM will equals to 46, but it should be 6 in hours and minutes.

Fixed: all of them internally consistent with each other.

7. On what day of the week are delays least likely?
```{r}
delay_by_day <- flights %>%
  mutate(day_of_week = wday(time_hour, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE),
         delayed = pmax(dep_delay, arr_delay, na.rm = TRUE) > 0)%>%
  group_by(day_of_week) %>%
  summarize(count = n(),
            proportion_delayed = sum(delayed, na.rm = TRUE) / count) %>%
  arrange(proportion_delayed)
head(delay_by_day,1)
```
The day have least delay is Saturday.



## General Social Survey

In the remainder of the exercises, we'll use a subset of the General Social Survey (GSS) dataset available in the `forcats` pacakges.

```{r load_gss}
data(gss_cat)
library(forcats)
library(dplyr)
```

Using the `gss_cat` dataset, use `fct_*` functions to accomplish the following tasks:

8. Make a plot that shows the relationship between marital status (`marital`) and `age` in a way that makes a trend clear.

```{r}
ggplot(gss_cat, aes(x = fct_reorder(marital, age, .fun = median, .na_rm = TRUE), y = age)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "Marital Status (Ordered by Median Age)", y = "Age",
       title = "Relationship between Marital Status and Age") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```






9. Make a plot that shows the relationship between religion followed (`relig`) and income `rincome`. Combine income categories for better readability.

```{r}
gss_cat_income <- gss_cat %>%
  mutate(rincome_combined = fct_collapse(
    rincome,
    "Unknow" =  c("No answer", "Don't know", "Refused"),
    "Low Income" = c("Lt $1000", "$1000 to 2999", "$3000 to 3999", "$4000 to 4999", "$5000 to 5999", "$6000 to 6999", "$7000 to 7999"),
    "Middle Income" = c("$8000 to 9999", "$10000 - 14999", "$15000 - 19999", "$20000 - 24999"),
    "High Income" = c("$25000 or more")
  ))%>%
  group_by(relig, rincome_combined) %>%
  summarise(count = n(),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(proportion = count / sum(count)) %>% 
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
ggplot(gss_cat_income, aes(x = relig, y = proportion, fill = rincome_combined)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +  
  labs(x = "Religion", y = "Proportion", fill = "Income Level",
       title = "Relationship between Religion and Income") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```
